monthly_review.summary: You've increased volume and intensity this month, with faster average pace and higher HR — indicating a meaningful shift toward more demanding aerobic work, though efficiency gains remain modest.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved (+0.20 m/sec per bpm) despite a 4 bpm rise in average HR — signaling better cardiovascular economy at similar or slightly higher intensities.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s total distance (51.5 vs 46.0 km) and need only 1 more run to match last month’s session count — aim for a 5–6 km Zone 2 run before month-end to maintain consistency without overloading.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite higher HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.62 m/sec per bpm while average HR increased 4 bpm — suggesting improved stroke volume or oxygen extraction, especially given stable VO2 max (37→38) and consistent vertical oscillation (~7.7 cm).

insights.title: Shift toward threshold and tempo work
insights.body: Zone 3 time jumped from 19% to 29%, and Zone 4 increased from 3% to 15% — a +12 percentage point rise in high-aerobic/low-anaerobic effort, aligning with faster average pace (536 → 551 sec/km) and elevated avg HR.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff under fatigue
insights.body: Cadence increased +5 spm (146→151), yet stride length dropped slightly (e.g., 69.73→68.77 in recent long runs) and ground contact time remained high (~314–317 ms), suggesting form tightness or neuromuscular fatigue during sustained efforts >10 km.

insights.title: Low-Z1 volume may limit recovery capacity
insights.body: Zone 1 dropped from 36% to 25% of total HR time — the lowest Z1 share in two months — and your easiest recent run (Jun 19) was only 3.2 km at 112 bpm (likely Z1), with no dedicated recovery sessions visible in the last 5 runs.

recommendations.action: Do one 5 km run at Zone 1 HR (≤125 bpm) before June 30, keeping cadence ≥145 spm and vertical oscillation ≤7.5 cm
recommendations.reason: Z1 volume is down 11% MoM and recent easy runs show elevated ground contact time (344 ms on Jun 19) — a true Z1 session will reinforce neuromuscular relaxation and improve recovery signaling.

recommendations.action: Add 10 seconds of walk break every 2 km during your next 10+ km run to reduce ground contact time by ≥10 ms
recommendations.reason: Ground contact averages 314–317 ms in all recent long runs (>10 km), above your personal baseline (274 ms on fast 3 km effort), indicating cumulative fatigue impact on form.

recommendations.action: Perform 3 sets of 60-second single-leg glute bridges (each leg) post-run on your next two moderate-effort days
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation is stable (7.7 cm) but ground contact time remains elevated — targeted glute activation improves pelvic stability and push-off efficiency, directly supporting stride length maintenance at fatigue.

weekly_focus.description: Balance continued aerobic stimulus with intentional recovery tactics to protect form, enhance efficiency gains, and avoid HR creep — especially critical as Zone 3/4 volume rises.
